chunks: And the Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he was asked about the ghusl of the deceased, and he said:

You begin by placing a cloth over his private parts, then sprinkle water over his chest and knees. Then begin and wash the head and beard with sidr until you cleanse it. Then begin with his right side, then his left side. If you wash his head and beard with khitmī, there is no harm. Pass your hand over his back and belly with one jar of water until you finish with them both. Then with a portion of camphor: place in the jar half a seed's measure of camphor, then wash his head and beard, then his right side, then his left side, and pass your hand over all of his body. Raise his head and beard somewhat, then pass your hand over his belly and squeeze it slightly until whatever comes out exits from its outlet. Let there be a cloth on your hands by which you clean his anus. Then incline his head somewhat and shake it so that whatever comes out from his nostril may come out. Then wash him with one jar of pure water; that makes three jars, and if you add more there is no harm. Insert into his seat some cotton, whatever can enter, then dry him with a clean cloth. Then wash your hands to the elbows and your legs to the knees. Then shroud him: begin and place upon his seat some cotton and dharīrah, and press his thighs tightly over it. Fumigate his garments with three sticks. Then begin and spread the wrapping sheet lengthwise, then sprinkle upon it some dharīrah, then the waist-wrapper lengthwise until it covers the chest and the legs, then the cloth, its width being about a span and a half, then the shirt. Tie the cloth over the shirt opposite the nakedness and the private part so that nothing of it appears. Put camphor in his hearing-places and on the traces of his sajdah from it and in it, and use less of the camphor. Place cotton upon his eyes and in them, and in his ears a small amount. Then turban him and cast dharīrah upon his face, and let the end of the turban hang down on his left side by the measure of a span, casting it upon his face. The one who washed him must perform ghusl, and everyone who touches a deceased person must perform ghusl, even if the deceased had already been washed. The shroud should be of burd cloth, and if it is not burd cloth then make all of it cotton. If you do not find a cotton turban, then make the turban sābirī.
And he said: “A woman needs for her front private part an amount of cotton equal to half a mann.”

And he said: “Takfīn is that you begin with the shirt, then the cloth above the shirt over his buttocks, his thighs, and his nakedness. You make the length of the cloth three cubits and a half, and its width a span and a half. Then you fasten the waist-wrapper in four places, then the wrapping sheet, then the turban upon his face. Place some camphor upon every garment, and scatter dharīrah upon his shroud.”
And he said: “If there is a tear in the wrapping sheet.”

And he said: “The first jar by which the deceased is washed is with sidr-water, the second jar is with camphor-water, in which camphor is crumbled in the amount of half a seed, and the third jar is with pure water.”

key_terms.التَّكْفِينُ: the shrouding of the deceased in burial cloths
key_terms.الذَّرِيرَةِ: powdered perfume sprinkled on the shroud
key_terms.السِّدْرِ: lotus-leaf preparation used in the first washing of the body
key_terms.اللِّفَافَةَ: the outer wrapping sheet of the shroud
key_terms.الْإِزَارَ: the waist-wrapper or lower shroud cloth
key_terms.الْكَافُورِ: camphor used in the second washing and in preparation of the deceased
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْمَيِّتِ: the ritual washing of the deceased
key_terms.مَاءِ الْقَرَاحِ: pure plain water used in the final washing

ai.seo_question: How is the deceased to be washed and shrouded according to this hadith from Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām?
ai.summary: This hadith details the procedure for the ghusl and takfīn of the deceased, including the order of washing, the use of sidr, camphor, and pure water, and the arrangement of the shroud. It also mentions related rulings such as ghusl becoming obligatory upon the one who washes or touches the deceased, and specific details concerning preparation materials and shrouding.
